title_en: The Glue That Failed Its Way to Success
title_zh: 失败的胶水，成功的便利贴
english_paragraphs: In 1968 Spencer Silver, a scientist at 3M, set out to make a super-strong adhesive. The polymer he produced did something else. Its tiny spheres formed a layer with little tack, giving paper a temporary hold, so it would adhere, peel off, and be reapplied. To an inventor chasing strength, the formulation was a setback.

For five years Silver acted as its promoter within 3M's corporate ranks, in informal chats and at seminars. In his own summary, it was a solution without a problem. His perseverance met indifference. The unconventional material found no use, and the pursuit proved fruitless.

In 1974 Art Fry, a colleague who had heard one of those talks, faced a small annoyance at church. The paper bookmarks wedged in his choir's hymn book kept getting dislodged and falling out. The frustration gave Fry an idea. The unwanted adhesive could make a marker that would cling to a page, stay put, and leave it undamaged.

In 1977 the notes were test-marketed as Press 'n Peel in four American cities, where purchasers showed little enthusiasm. In 1978 3M's marketers staged a blitz in Boise, Idaho, and dispensed complimentary packets of notes to offices. More than 90 per cent of respondents who tried them said they would buy. After the coolness came a turnaround.

On 6 April 1980 the pads, rebranded as Post-it Notes, went on sale nationally in the US, and Canada and Europe followed in 1981. The stationery staple owes its signature canary tone to an unplanned twist. The laboratory next door had only leftover yellow paper.
chinese_source_paragraphs: 1968年，斯潘塞·西尔弗，3M公司的一位科学家，**着手**(set out to)研制一种**超强**(super-strong)**黏合剂**(adhesive)。然而他制成的**聚合物**(polymer)却做了**其他的事情**(something else)。它的微小的**球状颗粒**(spheres)形成一层**黏着力**(tack)很小的涂层，让纸张获得**暂时的**(temporary)黏着，因此纸张能**粘附**(adhere)上去，**揭下**(peel off)后还能**重新贴上**(reapplied)。对一个追求强度的**发明者**(inventor)来说，这种**配方**(formulation)是一次**挫折**(setback)。

五年间，西尔弗在3M的**企业**(corporate)上下**充当**(acted as)它的**推广者**(promoter)，在**非正式的**(informal)闲谈中、也在**研讨会**(seminars)上介绍它。用他自己的话**总结**(summary)，这完全是一个**解决**(solution)“不存在的问题”的**方案**(solution)。他的**坚持不懈**(perseverance)换来的是**冷漠**(indifference)。这种**非常规的**(unconventional)材料**找不到用途**(found no use)，这番**追求**(pursuit)终究**一无所获**(fruitless)。

1974年，阿特·弗莱，一位听过其中一次讲座的同事，在教堂里遇到了一件小小的**烦心事**(annoyance)。他所在**唱诗班**(choir)的**赞美诗**(hymn)集里**夹着的**(wedged)纸**书签**(bookmarks)总是**移位**(dislodged)，**掉出来**(falling out)。这份**懊恼**(frustration)让弗莱想到一个主意。这种**没人要的**(unwanted)黏合剂可以做成一种书签，**附着在**(cling to)书页上**不会移动**(stay put)，还能让书页**完好无损**(undamaged)。

1977年，这种**便条**(notes)以 Press 'n Peel 之名在美国四个城市**试销**(test-marketed)，然而在这四个城市，**购买者**(purchasers)展示出极少的**热情**(enthusiasm)。1978年，3M的**营销人员**(marketers)在爱达荷州博伊西**发起**(staged)一场**闪电攻势**(blitz)，向很多办公室**分发**(dispensed)**免费的**(complimentary)一**小包**(packets)一小包的便条。试用过的**受访者**(respondents)中，超过90%表示会购买。**冷遇**(coolness)之后，迎来了**转机**(turnaround)。

1980年4月6日，这种**便笺本**(pads)**更名为**(rebranded as)**便利贴**(Post-it Notes)，在美国**全国**(nationally)上市；1981年，便利贴又进入加拿大和欧洲。这款**文具的**(stationery)**必备品**(staple)那**标志性的**(signature)**金丝雀黄**(canary)**色调**(tone)，源于一次**计划外的**(unplanned)转折。因为当时隔壁的实验室里，只有一些**剩余的**(leftover)黄纸。

sentences.chinese_source: 这款**文具的**(stationery)**必备品**(staple)那**标志性的**(signature)**金丝雀黄**(canary)**色调**(tone)，源于一次**计划外的**(unplanned)转折。

sentences.english: The laboratory next door had only leftover yellow paper.
sentences.chinese_source: 因为当时隔壁的实验室里，只有一些**剩余的**(leftover)黄纸。

approved_summary: 1968年，3M的西尔弗想造超强胶，却做出由微小球粒组成的弱黏胶，纸张能贴住、揭下再贴。
他在公司推广多年后，同事弗莱于1974年想到，用这种胶固定总从赞美诗集中滑落的书签，且不伤书页。
1977年，这种便条在美国四个城市试销，消费者反应冷淡。
1978年，3M在博伊西向办公室免费发试用品；试用过的受访者中，超过九成表示愿意购买。
1980年，产品改名“便利贴”在全美上市，次年进入加拿大和欧洲；标志性的黄色，仅因隔壁实验室剩下黄纸。
